key_insight: EdgeRefine improves the privacy-utility trade-off for graph learning by using Jaccard-based edge ranking and selective sampling to preserve useful structure while satisfying edge differential privacy.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to deploy GNNs on sensitive graphs with less accuracy loss than uniform noise injection, making private graph analytics more feasible.
method: Estimate edge-existence likelihood with Jaccard similarity and rank edges for refinement.
Use privacy budget ε to control the ratio of true vs. false edges sampled.
Apply a separate sampling rate k to cap graph size and maintain sparsity.
evidence_signal: Across multiple datasets and GNNs, EdgeRefine matches or approaches non-private performance and outperforms prior privacy-preserving baselines, including gains of 17.8% on ACM with GAT and 19.7% on Cora with GCN at ε=2.5.
watch_item: The method depends on reliable similarity-based edge ranking and careful tuning of ε and k, which may be sensitive to graph homophily and dataset structure.
paper_title: EdgeRefine: Privacy-Utility Balance for Graphs via Jaccard Sampling under Edge Differential Privacy
